changes: New: Automatic Transcoding via Adobe Media Encoder

Clips or effects DaVinci Resolve can't reproduce natively - unsupported Video/Audio Effects, Time Remapping, Masks/Mask AI, Adjustment Layers with an effect, After Effects Dynamic Link (.aep) and After Effects Graphics (.aegraphic) clips, Titles/Graphics with alpha - are now automatically rendered through Adobe Media Encoder before conversion, so the visual/audio result is preserved instead of lost
Fully configurable: enable/disable Transcoding entirely, or toggle each clip category independently
Choose the output folder and the filename suffix used for transcoded media
Transitions (e.g. a Cross Dissolve) between a transcoded clip and its neighbor are preserved by baking the transition directly into the transcoded clip
Cineform RGB 12-bit / GoPro Cineform RGB 16-bit is only offered as an Encoding Preset on Windows, since it's not available on macOS
New: Return to Premiere

Once clips have been color graded in DaVinci Resolve (a Color Node applied), CrossFlow can now detect them, export them out of Resolve, and automatically build a new Premiere Pro project with the graded clips already placed back in
Started directly from a past conversion in the new Results tab, with a confirmation step before running
Choose the exported clips' filename suffix and the new project's save location
New: Results tab with full Task History
Every conversion, and every Return to Premiere run, is now saved and reviewable later, including after closing and reopening CrossFlow
See the full source project analysis, the options used, and a detailed per-clip breakdown of what was converted, transcoded, or flagged (warnings/errors), with rendered file reasons and sizes
Live progress is shown in the Results tab while a task is running
Delete past results you no longer need
New: Notifications and progress tracking
Native OS notification when a process finishes (can be disabled in Settings & License)
Taskbar (Windows) / Dock (macOS) icon now shows a live progress bar for the running process
CrossFlow automatically comes back to the front if Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve steal window focus while a process is running, without interrupting a dialog you need to interact with in either app
New Transferable item: Warp Stabilizer
Clips with the Warp Stabilizer effect applied are now transferred, with DaVinci Resolve's own Stabilization applied to match
New Transferable item: Track Mute and Solo
Timeline tracks that are Muted (Video and Audio) or Soloed (Audio) in Premiere Pro now keep that same state on the converted DaVinci Resolve timeline
Now officially supporting DaVinci Resolve 21.0.3
Reliability improvements
Premiere Pro is launched independently from CrossFlow, so closing CrossFlow doesn	 close Premiere Pro mid-process
Various fixes around transcoding and replacing clips back into the project (audio track mute/unmute handling, filename/import edge cases, AI Mask detection)
Fixed a replaced Title/Graphic sometimes leaving a leftover, overlapping clip behind on the timeline instead of being fully replaced
Clips with animated (keyframed) Position, Scale, Rotation, Anchor Point, Opacity, Volume, or Pan are now properly preserved via Automatic Transcoding instead of silently losing the animation
Interface improvements
Redesigned results/feedback screens with clearer icons and before/after project indications
Options and buttons are hidden while a process is running, to keep the interface focused on progress
New background interactive look, can be disabled from the Settings tab
A lot more to come: keep sending your feedback at contact.crossflow@gmail.com, it directly shapes what gets built next!
First Release of CrossFlow
Windows 11 and Mac from 12.0 supported
Adobe Premiere Pro projects created from 13.0 (Premiere Pro CC 2019)
DaVinci Resolve Studio from 20.0 (not tested in Beta 21.X yet)
Note: CrossFlow does not work with the Free DaVinci Resolve Standard version
Supported while converting your Premiere Pro Project to DaVinci Resolve:
Multiple Timelines with different Framerates or Resolutions
Different Timeline Audio Tracks Config (Mono, Stereo, 5.1, ..)
Nested Sequences
Multicam Sequences
Timeline Clip classical effects, such as Opacity, BlendMode, Position, Scale, Anchor, Audio Volume, Pan, ..
Timeline Clip Speed Changed and/or Reversed
Timeline Clip Name and Colors
Some Audio and Video Transitions
Framerate Interpreted Footages
Image Sequences and Hold Frames
Project Bin Folder Structures
Project Item and Timeline Markers
A lot more to come: I need your input to know where I should focus!
